name: cc-enforcer
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, ten of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.39.2 makes the Stop hook read the transcript's tail instead of the whole file. stop_guard._last_assistant_message_from_transcript used read_text() + splitlines() on the session JSONL to find the last text-bearing assistant entry; on 2026-09-15 a 2.5 GB transcript turned every Stop into a 12.7 GB process for six seconds (available RAM 19.9 GB -> 1.7 GB) and Windows paged out the user's other services — a 90 s backend stall per turn, from a hook whose whole job is to run unnoticed. The reader now walks the file backwards in growing byte windows (4 MiB, x4, capped at 64 MiB) cut to whole lines and returns the first text-bearing assistant entry it meets: the same answer as before at a peak cost of a few windows — measured on the 2.5 GB file itself, 8.3 MB traced peak in 0.02 s. Three tests pin it: a 60 MB transcript costs under four windows, a line longer than the window grows it, and 256-byte windows agree with a whole-file scan. 746 -> 749 tests. Prior — v0.39.1 is a documentation release with one gate behind it, and the gate's first finding closed. Pinning only the newest CHANGELOG heading against plugin.json answers the bump-vs-entry question and nothing else: the headings under it are unchecked, so a release that got its entry and its release: commit while the tag was never cut sat in the file with every gate green. tests/test_version_sync.py now compares the whole released set against git tag, and the first thing it named was this repository's own 0.38.2 — a heading and a release: commit with no tag underneath them, so there was nothing to install at that point in history, gh release view answered 'release not found', and the repository front page kept naming an older version as Latest. Closing it was a release-time action rather than a code change: v0.38.2 is now an annotated tag on its release commit carrying a GitHub release built from its own entry, so v0.38.1 -> v0.38.2 -> v0.38.3 is a complete sequence and the gate is green on the fact rather than on a waiver. Two versions are excused, and only because their own entries say so where readers see it: 0.8.0 was rolled into the v0.9.0 commit, and 0.25.1 was released inside the v0.26.0 commit that also wrote its heading. UNTAGGED_BY_RECORD registers them, a companion test re-derives that declaration from the CHANGELOG entry itself, and the registration has to end the day a tag appears — the registry cannot excuse a version the record has not admitted in public. CI checks out with fetch-depth: 0, because the default depth-1 checkout brings no tags and the gate would have nothing to read; the suite reads that line out of the workflow, since a shallow clone makes the tag check skip itself and would otherwise let a green run stand over a gate that inspected nothing. Both plugin descriptions and both READMEs were aligned with the code in the same pass: twelve rules with ten backed by a hook, and four CI drift gates, the demo gate named beside the version, doc and i18n ones. 742 -> 746 tests. Prior — v0.39.0 thins the injected contract, because it had been eating the feature it was supposed to leave room for. v0.38.3 fixed the symptom — edicts dropped silently on a long install path; this is the cause. The SessionStart contract had grown to 9,262 characters against a 10,000-character hook cap and nothing gated it: 991 characters of headroom at v0.29, 914 at v0.32, 552 at v0.35, by which point a real install path plus two real edicts no longer fit and a headline feature was degrading to nothing in the field. It is now 6,627 characters with 3,373 of headroom. What came out was duplication, not text: section 2's Recovery column, every word of which is printed at deny time in the block reason's own recovery section, and section 1's paragraph rows, whose heading already calls it a one-line index — each concept checked against prompts/user-prompt.md, re-injected EVERY turn, before being cut. Three tokens that lived only in the Recovery column were folded into the trigger cells rather than dropped. Three things the first pass cut that lived nowhere else at cold start went back in, caught by the tests that assert them: the four self-quiz questions verbatim and the layer (e) / layer (f) consequence for rules 08 and 09. The zh mirror got the same treatment, because a mirror that stops mirroring is how the deny set came to differ between languages in v0.26. The gate: a 120-character install root plus three edicts rendered by the real renderer must survive in both languages with no elision — ordinary parameters, named in the test, verified RED against the pre-thinning contract. 741 -> 742 tests (v0.39.0). Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
